name: Jain
blurb: A Hindu-looking wedding with a different rulebook underneath: the offerings go to the Tirthankaras, the chants come from Jain scripture, and non-violence shapes the menu, the flowers and the guest list.

events.name: Lagna Lekhan
events.description: A small puja at the bride's home at which the auspicious date and time are written down and formally fixed. Close family attend. Everything else in the plan hangs off the date settled here.

events.name: Sagai — the engagement
events.description: The formal engagement, with gifts exchanged between the families and often a tilak for the groom.

events.name: Mandap Mahurat and Griha Shanti
events.description: Prayers at both homes before the wedding structures go up, asking for the removal of obstacles and peace on the household.

events.name: Bana Betai — the paste ceremony
events.description: The equivalent of haldi, but the paste is made from chickpea flour rather than turmeric in many Jain families. Married women of the family apply it to the bride and groom at their own homes.

events.name: Mehndi
events.description: Henna for the bride and the women of both families, with music and food. Cultural rather than religious, and near-universal in Gujarati Jain families.

events.name: Sangeet
events.description: The big musical night — rehearsed dances from both families, and usually the largest party of the week after the wedding itself.

events.name: Barat and Sanmuk Milap
events.description: The groom's procession arrives and the two families formally meet and embrace. Jain barats are typically without alcohol and often without the horse.

events.name: The vivah vidhi
events.description: The ceremony itself: the granthi bandhan tying the couple's garments, the hasta melap joining of hands, and the pheras around the sacred fire. The offerings and chants are Jain, drawn from texts such as the Acar Dinkar, and are addressed to the Tirthankaras rather than to Hindu deities.

events.name: Vidaai
events.description: The bride's farewell to her family. Emotional, brief, and traditionally the point at which she leaves for the groom's home.

events.name: Reception
events.when: Wedding evening or the following day
events.description: Hosted by the groom's family in most Jain communities. Strictly vegetarian, and in observant families without root vegetables.

events.name: Temple visit
events.description: The couple visit the derasar to offer prayers, often the day after.

items.name: Pandit or vidhikar fee
items.note: Ask specifically for someone who performs the Jain vidhi rather than the Hindu one. The structure looks similar but the mantras, the offerings and the number of pheras differ.

items.name: Lagna Lekhan and muhurat consultation
items.note: The date and time are fixed at this puja and everything else follows. Book the astrologer before the venue.

items.name: Mandap hire and decoration
items.note: The canopy over the sacred fire. Experienced mandap companies handle the venue's fire permissions, which is a good reason to use one.

items.name: Puja items and havan samagri
items.note: Everything the fire needs. Jain families often ask for the offerings to exclude honey and certain items — confirm with the vidhikar rather than the general supplier.

items.name: Derasar donation
items.note: Where the ceremony or a blessing happens at the temple.

items.name: Varmala garlands
items.note: Made fresh on the morning. Some strict Jain families prefer fabric or beaded garlands, since picking flowers harms living plants.

items.name: Civil marriage notice and registration
items.note: In England and Wales the Jain ceremony alone usually has no legal effect, because most banqueting venues are not registered for marriage.

items.name: Ceremony venue hire
items.note: Ask about open flame for the fire before anything else.

items.name: Reception venue hire
items.note: Often the same venue as the ceremony, sometimes grander and on a different day.

items.name: Wedding day catering
items.note: Strictly vegetarian. Many observant Jain families also exclude root vegetables — onion, garlic, potato, carrot — because harvesting them kills the plant and the soil organisms around it. This is a competence, not a menu tick-box.

items.name: Catering for mehndi, sangeet and bana betai
items.note: Three or four separate events, each fed. This line is why a Jain wedding budget is not one wedding.

items.name: Soft drinks, mocktails and juices
items.note: Jain weddings are alcohol-free. Spend the drinks budget on something interesting rather than jugs of squash.

items.name: Bridal outfit
items.note: Panetar and gharchola in Gujarati Jain families. Made to order from India needs months plus shipping, customs and alterations. Ask about silk — some Jain families avoid it, since traditional silk production kills the silkworm.

items.name: Outfits for the other events
items.note: Bana betai, mehndi, sangeet, reception. Four outfits is normal, not indulgent.

items.name: Groom's outfit
items.note: Sherwani or dhoti-kurta, same lead times and fittings.

items.name: Jewellery
items.note: Gold given to the bride is security and a family statement, not decoration. Budget it as a line.

items.name: Mehndi artist
items.note: Bridal mehndi takes three to eight hours and the stain needs a day to deepen. Nothing else can share that day.

items.name: Hair and make-up across the events
items.note: Several events, several looks, often starting before dawn to hit the muhurat.

items.name: Photographer
items.note: Must have shot a Jain or Gujarati wedding before. The key moments — granthi bandhan, hasta melap, the pheras — are quiet and easily missed in a loud room.

items.name: Videographer
items.note: Worth it for the vidhi itself, which is long, quiet and easily lost in a loud room.

items.name: Sangeet DJ, sound and staging
items.note: The biggest party of the week for most families.

items.name: Sangeet choreographer
items.note: Six weeks of rehearsals with both families. Book before the outfits.

items.name: Dhol players for the barat
items.note: The barat always runs late. Build slack between its start and the muhurat.

items.name: Flowers and styling
items.note: Confirm with the family whether fresh flowers are used, or fabric alternatives.

items.name: Invitations
items.note: Say plainly that the event is vegetarian and alcohol-free, and whether root vegetables are excluded, so guests and their dietary needs are not a surprise.

items.name: Transport
items.note: Getting both families between homes, ceremony and reception across several days.

items.name: Gifts between the families
items.note: Exchanged at the sagai and again at the wedding. Substantial and expected.

items.name: Daan — charitable giving
items.note: Giving is built into Jain practice, and many families make a significant donation as part of the wedding rather than as an afterthought.

items.name: Contingency
items.note: Hold something back. A week-long wedding with a fixed muhurat and several venues generates surprises that a one-day wedding does not.

timeline.task: Fix the muhurat through the Lagna Lekhan before booking anything — the auspicious time anchors every other booking
Find a pandit or vidhikar who performs the Jain vidhi specifically, not the Hindu one
Book the venue, and get written permission for an open flame indoors for the fire
Establish with both families whether root vegetables are excluded, and how strictly — it decides which caterers are even possible
Decide the civil plan now: a Jain ceremony in England and Wales usually has no legal effect on its own
Book a caterer who cooks Jain food properly, not an Indian caterer who will 'leave out the onion'
Book the mandap company and let them handle the venue's fire safety between them
Order the bridal outfit and the groom's — months, plus shipping, customs and alterations
Ask about silk and about flower garlands, since some families avoid both on ahimsa grounds
Book the photographer and videographer who have shot a Jain or Gujarati wedding
Book the DJ and the choreographer, and set the sangeet rehearsal dates with both families
Confirm the guest list across all events — the sangeet and reception lists are usually different and both larger than you think
Book the mehndi artist and block the whole day before the wedding for the bride
Plan the outfits for bana betai, mehndi and sangeet
Send invitations stating clearly that the events are vegetarian and alcohol-free
Give notice for the civil marriage
Arrange the Mandap Mahurat and Griha Shanti at both homes
Print a programme or brief an emcee to explain the vidhi as it goes, since much of the room will not know the Jain differences
Confirm the puja items with the vidhikar, including anything the family wishes to exclude
Build thirty to sixty minutes of slack between the barat's arrival and the muhurat
Confirm final numbers with a buffer rather than an exact count
Walk the run of the day against the muhurat with the pandit
Confirm the fire permission and the smoke detector arrangements in writing
Register the civil marriage and collect the certificate

paperwork.note: In England and Wales a Jain ceremony in a banqueting hall or marquee has no legal effect on its own, because the venue is not registered for marriage. Couples who skip this are legally unmarried, which surfaces years later in property, inheritance and immigration.

paperwork.item: Passports or birth certificates and proof of address
Evidence of the ending of any previous marriage
Written venue permission for an open flame
paperwork.note: Specific to the havan, with a fire-safe mandap setup and an agreement about smoke detectors. Get it before the deposit, not after.

paperwork.item: Registration after the ceremony in India
paperwork.note: Registration under the Hindu Marriage Act covers Jains, Buddhists and Sikhs as well. Courts have held that you need both the rites and the certificate.
If you want the legal ceremony at the venue rather than the register office. Registrars book out earlier than venues.

paperwork.item: Confirmation of the caterer's Jain provision in writing
paperwork.note: Put the root-vegetable question in the contract. Verbal agreement with a sales manager is not the same as the kitchen understanding it.

paperwork.item: Council or police permission for a street procession
paperwork.note: If the barat goes along a public road. Some venues also ban animals outright.

customs.name: The offerings are Jain, not Hindu
customs.description: The structure of the ceremony resembles a Gujarati Hindu wedding, but the offerings are made to the Tirthankaras and the mantras derive from Jain texts such as the Acar Dinkar. Booking a pandit who performs the Hindu vidhi and assuming it is close enough is the most common mistake.

customs.name: Granthi bandhan
customs.description: The bride's sari end and the groom's shawl are tied together in a knot before the pheras, so the couple are physically joined for the circling.

customs.name: The pheras
customs.description: Sources and communities differ on the number: some Jain communities take four pheras, others seven as in Gujarati Hindu practice, and Svetambara and Digambara custom is not uniform. Ask your own vidhikar and your family rather than working from a general guide.

customs.name: Bana Betai
customs.description: The paste ceremony that stands in for haldi. In many Jain families the paste is chickpea flour without turmeric, applied at each home by the married women of the family.

customs.name: Ahimsa shapes the day
customs.description: Non-violence is not an abstraction here. It reaches the menu, sometimes the flowers, sometimes the silk, and the absence of alcohol. Families vary in strictness, and the two sides may not match.

customs.name: No root vegetables, in observant families
customs.description: Onion, garlic, potato and carrot are avoided because uprooting the plant kills it and the organisms in the soil. Many caterers who advertise Jain food do not actually cook this way.

customs.name: Alcohol-free
customs.description: Jain weddings do not serve alcohol. This is settled rather than negotiable, and worth saying on the invitation.

customs.name: Daan
customs.description: Charitable giving is woven into the occasion rather than added to it, and many families give substantially at the time of a wedding.

customs.name: Digambara and Svetambara
customs.description: The two main traditions share the principles and differ in some practice. A vidhikar from one will usually say so if asked, and mixed marriages between them are common and unremarkable.

customs.name: Vidaai
customs.description: The bride's departure. Brief, and the moment most families find hardest.

customs.name: Chaturmas
customs.description: The four monsoon months are a period of restraint and study in which many families avoid weddings. Dates shift with the lunar calendar.

gotchas: Jain is not a subset of Hindu. Booking a Hindu pandit, a Hindu-format ceremony or a caterer who treats Jain food as 'Indian vegetarian' produces a wedding that the family will recognise as wrong.
The root vegetable question decides your caterer, not your menu. Ask both families how strictly they observe it before you shortlist anyone, and put the answer in the contract.
The number of pheras genuinely varies between Jain communities. Do not settle it from a website. Ask your vidhikar and both families, well before the programme is printed.
The havan means real fire indoors. Many Western venues refuse open flames or handle them badly. You need written permission, a fire-safe mandap and an agreement about smoke detectors.
In England and Wales the ceremony alone usually has no legal effect, because banqueting halls and marquees are not registered for marriage. Decide the civil plan at the start.
Alcohol is not a negotiation. Non-Jain guests and non-Jain in-laws sometimes assume there will be a bar 'just for the reception'. Say it on the invitation.
Silk and fresh flowers are a question in stricter families, because traditional silk production kills the silkworm and cut flowers are living things. Ask before you order the varmala.
The wedding is not one event. Bana betai, mehndi, sangeet, the wedding and the reception each need feeding, staffing and outfits. Budget for the week, not the day.
Bridal mehndi takes three to eight hours and the stain needs a day to deepen. Nothing that needs her hands can share that day.
The barat always runs late, and the muhurat does not move. Build thirty to sixty minutes of slack and tell the photographer where the pause will be.
Chaturmas closes several months for weddings in observant families, and the dates move with the lunar calendar each year.
